classification.difficultyReason: Read a marked point from each supplied reciprocal graph, calculate k=xy and identify the two coordinate-axis asymptotes; both parts directly apply the taught graph model.

content.prompt: Write down the equations of the graphs shown and identify the asymptotes.

spec.description: Left member of the supplied two-graph row. Positive reciprocal branches with continuation arrows, x and y axes, no grid, and dashed guides locating x=3 and y=1. Source blue is normalised to the standard graph blue.
spec.mathematics: Reciprocal graph through (3,1), with coordinate-axis asymptotes; equation withheld from student-facing labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes, branches and reading guides are permanent question givens; no equation is printed.

answer.worked:
The marked point is $(3,1)$. For $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$,
$$\begin{align*}k&=xy\\k&=3\times1\\k&=3\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=\dfrac{3}{x}$. The branches approach the coordinate axes, so the asymptotes are $x=0$ and $y=0$.

spec.description: Right member of the supplied two-graph row. Negative reciprocal branches with continuation arrows, x and y axes, no grid, and dashed guides locating x=-2 and y=2. Source blue is normalised to the standard graph blue.
spec.mathematics: Reciprocal graph through (-2,2), with coordinate-axis asymptotes; equation withheld from student-facing labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes, branches and reading guides are permanent question givens; no equation is printed.

answer.worked:
The marked point is $(-2,2)$. For $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$,
$$\begin{align*}k&=xy\\k&=(-2)\times2\\k&=-4\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=-\dfrac{4}{x}$. The branches approach the coordinate axes, so the asymptotes are $x=0$ and $y=0$.
